title: How to Calculate Relative Mass
page_title: How to Calculate Relative Mass | Edexcel IGCSE Science (Double Award) (Modular) Revision Notes 2024

blocks.name: Relative Formula Mass & Relative Molecular Mass

blocks.text: How to calculate relative formula mass

blocks.md:
- The symbol for the relative atomic mass is *A*<sub>*r*</sub>
- This is calculated from the **mass number** and **relative abundances** of all the **isotopes** of a particular element
- The symbol for the relative formula mass is *M*<sub>*r*</sub> and it refers to the** total mass** of the molecule
- To calculate the *M*<sub>*r*</sub> of a substance, you have to add up the **relative atomic masses** of all the atoms present in the formula

- In accordance with the [Law of Conservation of Mass](https://www.savemyexams.com/igcse/science/edexcel/double-award-modular/24/chemistry-unit-1/revision-notes/principles-of-chemistry/chemical-formulae-equations-calculations/chemical-equations/), the sum of the relative formula masses of the reactants will be the same as the sum of the relative formula masses of the products

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
Calculate the relative formula mass of:

1. Sodium chloride, NaCl
2. Copper oxide, CuO
3. Magnesium nitrate, Mg(NO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>

**Final answer:** **Answers:**

1. Sodium chloride

  - NaCl = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5
2. Copper oxide

  - CuO = 63.5 + 16 = 79.5
3. Magnesium nitrate

  - Mg(NO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub> = 24 + (14 x 1 x 2) + (16 x 3 x 2) = 148

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: The relative atomic mass of every element is given on the Periodic Table. It is the larger of the two numbers.
